questions.q: Which database table stores every Business Rule in a ServiceNow instance?
options: sys_script
sys_ui_policy
sys_data_policy
sys_security_acl
questions.explain: Business Rules are rows on sys_script, regardless of which table they target.

questions.q: A Business Rule can be configured to run on which combination of events?
options: Insert, update, delete, and query
Only on form submit
Only when a user clicks a UI Action button
Only on scheduled job execution
questions.explain: Business Rules react to database events — insert, update, delete, and query — not to a user manually triggering them.

questions.q: Look at this Business Rule body. What triggers this script to run?
options: The platform calling it automatically when a matching database operation happens on the rule's target table
A user clicking a 'Run Script' related link on the form
A scheduled job that runs once per day
The browser executing it when the page finishes loading
questions.explain: Business Rule scripts are invoked automatically by the server whenever a database event matching the rule's configuration occurs — no explicit call is needed.

questions.q: Why are Business Rules considered more powerful than UI Policies?
options: They run on the server with full GlideRecord access to any table, not just client-side field visibility on one form
UI Policies cannot be activated or deactivated
Business Rules only affect the field currently in focus
UI Policies and Business Rules are functionally identical
questions.explain: A UI Policy only controls what's visible or mandatory in the browser; a Business Rule runs server-side and can read or write any table in the instance.

questions.q: What makes Business Rules the most dangerous automation mechanism on the platform, per this lesson?
options: A careless one runs on every matching save, at scale, in production, with full server access
They require a special license that most instances don't have
They can only be written by ServiceNow support staff
They never actually execute unless manually triggered by an administrator
questions.explain: Because Business Rules fire automatically and run with full server-side reach, a mistake doesn't stay contained to one record or one form — it repeats across every matching save.
